## GET /admin-api/federation

`getFederationRelationships`

**Every federation relationship, in either direction**

This service can be EITHER END of a federation relationship, in five protocols: SAML 2.0, SAML 1.1, WS-Federation 1.2, OpenID Connect and OAuth 2.0.

**This is the one feature here that has to be configured before it will do anything.** Everywhere else this service accepts what it is given — any username, any client_id, any entityID, any LDAP bind. It cannot do that at an assertion consumer service: what arrives there is an unauthenticated HTTP request claiming to be a person, and the session it produces is the same one `/oauth2/authorize`, `/wsfed`, `/saml2` and the admin console all read. So a relationship is created DISABLED, and an assertion is refused unless it verifies against the certificate configured on it.

**And the gate is on the SUBJECT too (#109).** A partner signs in only the person its (issuer, subject) is linked to — a `federationLink` on the entry — and what happens to a subject nobody linked is the relationship's `fedSubjectPolicy`: a local sign-in as the person it names before linking (`link-at-first-sign-in`, the default), a refusal (`pre-linked`), a new namespaced entry (`jit-namespaced`), or, in development only, the old name match (`any-existing`). `fedSubjectGroup`, `fedSubjectDomain` and `fedSubjectPattern` narrow it further, and a console administrator is refused unless `fedMayAssertAdministrators` is on.

`?relationship=<id>` returns one of them, with everything it holds and the URLs to configure at the partner. It answers 200 with `found: false` for an id that is not registered.

This resource holds nothing: every row is an entry under `ou=federations`, the same one an `ldapsearch` reads.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/federation` on the admin console.

The reply also carries `protocolEndpoints`: every endpoint of this family in the realm the call arrived in, as `{ name, methods, url }` (plus `route` for an HTTP endpoint, `transport` for a socket, and `registered: false` for a route the router no longer has).

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `relationship` | query | string |  | One relationship, by its id. |
| `q` | query | string |  | Filter the list by id, name, partner or application. |
| `role` | query | one of `service-provider`, `identity-provider` |  | Only the relationships in which this service takes that role. `service-provider` is the direction that CONSUMES somebody else's assertions. |
| `category` | query | one of `enterprise`, `consumer` |  | Only the enterprise partners, or only the consumer and social providers (#565): a relationship that names a `provider` is consumer. |
| `page` | query | integer |  | Which page of the match to return. CLAMPED rather than refused: a page past the end returns the last one, and the reply says which page it actually is. |
| `per` | query | integer |  | Rows per page. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 300. On a drill-down it is SHARED by every list in the reply, which each carry a page number of their own. |
| `linksPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `links` to return, answered by `linksPaging`. With `relationship`: the people whose federationLink is through it (#109), each `{ username, dn, link, issuer, subject }`. |
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

## POST /admin-api/federation/add-value

`addFederationValue`

**Add a value to a multi-valued field**

Any multi-valued field: the relationship's own `editable` table marks them, and this operation's `field` lists them. A field holding one value is refused rather than assigned (#747). Two have rules of their own.

**`fedAttributeMap`** is written `<incoming name>=<LDAP attribute>` and is split at the FIRST equals sign — which matters, because an incoming name can be a URL and a URL can hold one. It is only needed for a partner's own inventions: the ordinary OpenID Connect claims, the SAML `urn:oid:` names and the AD FS claim URIs are mapped already.

**`fedRelease`** names an attribute or claim released to that partner, and it can only REMOVE — from what /admin/claims, /admin/saml-attributes and the groups claim would add, and from nothing else. It cannot touch `sub`, `iss`, `exp` or a NameID. **NO VALUES MEANS NO POLICY, not release nothing**: adding the first value here is what starts the filtering.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/federation` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `field` | one of `description`, `fedAllowedTenants`, `fedAuthorizeParams`, `fedAttributeMap`, `fedSubjectGroup`, `fedSubjectDomain`, `fedHomeRealmDomain`, `fedSignalsEvents`, `fedRelease` | yes | Which list. |
| `id` | string | yes | The relationship. |
| `value` | string | yes | The value to add. |

**200**: The relationship with the value added.

## POST /admin-api/federation/check-partner

`checkFederationPartner`

**Check an OpenID Connect partner's configuration**

Service-provider-side OpenID Connect relationships only (#930). Fetches what a sign-in would: the partner's discovery document where `fedDiscovery` is on — its issuer held to `fedPeer` — and its key set, and answers the endpoints and how many keys this service can read. Writes nothing and signs nobody in.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/federation` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | The relationship. |

**200**: `issuer`, `endpoints`, `discovered`, `keys` and `readable`.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `discovered` | boolean |  |  |
| `endpoints` | object |  |  |
| `endpoints.authorization_endpoint` | string |  |  |
| `endpoints.jwks_uri` | string |  |  |
| `endpoints.token_endpoint` | string |  |  |
| `endpoints.userinfo_endpoint` | string |  |  |
| `errors` | list |  |  |
| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `issuer` | string |  |  |
| `keys` | integer |  |  |
| `message` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean | yes |  |
| `readable` | integer |  |  |
| `why` | string |  |  |

**400**: The operation was refused; `errors` says why and nothing changed.

## POST /admin-api/federation/create

`createFederationRelationship`

**Register a federation relationship**

It is created **DISABLED**, whatever this request says, and nothing about it does anything until `enable` is called. That is the one place this operation overrides its input, and it is deliberate: a partner that half-exists and silently accepts assertions is the failure this whole register is arranged to prevent, so enabling is a second act that says the configuration is finished.

**ONE RELATIONSHIP IS ONE DIRECTION.** A partner this service both consumes from and asserts to is two relationships with two ids, because everything that configures one differs by direction.

The reply carries `readiness.missing` — the fields this protocol and role still need — so a caller can go straight on to `set` for each of them without knowing the schema in advance.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/federation` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `application` | string |  | On an identity-provider-side relationship only: the identifier of the partner's entry in `ou=applications`. Its entityID, redirect URIs and certificate stay THERE, where every protocol module reads them — this register holds a pointer and not a copy. |
| `clientId` | string |  | With `provider`: this service's client_id at the provider, set as `fedClientId` in the same act. |
| `clientSecret` | string |  | With `provider`: this service's secret at the provider, set as `fedClientSecret` in the same act and sealed as that field always is. Never echoed. |
| `id` | string | yes | The key, the RDN and a URL segment. It has to start with a letter or a digit and hold only letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore, up to 63 characters. |
| `name` | string |  | What to call the partner on a page. The id is the name when this is omitted. |
| `peer` | string |  | The partner's own identifier — a SAML entityID, an OpenID Connect issuer, a WS-Federation wtrealm. On a service-provider-side relationship it is CHECKED: an assertion whose issuer is not this string is refused even when the signature verifies. |
| `protocol` | one of `saml2`, `saml11`, `wsfed`, `oidc`, `oauth2`, `ssf` | yes | The protocol the relationship runs in. `ssf` (#374) is a partner that signs nobody in and only sends Shared Signals; it takes the service-provider role. |
| `provider` | one of `google`, `discord`, `github`, `microsoft`, `microsoft-any`, `linkedin`, `yahoo`, `slack`, `twitch`, `salesforce`, `facebook`, `amazon`, `spotify`, `x`, `tiktok`, `apple`, `gitlab`, `gitlab-self-managed`, `bitbucket`, `patreon`, `roblox`, `battlenet`, `epic`, `paypal`, `dropbox`, `box`, `steam`, `codeberg`, `gitea`, `huggingface`, `asana`, `atlassian`, `replit`, `mastodon`, `sourceforge`, `stackoverflow`, `oschina`, `discourse`, `bluesky`, `generic-oidc`, `generic-oauth2` |  | A CONSUMER OR SOCIAL PROVIDER (#565): the profile the relationship is made from. Its endpoints, issuer, scope and token authentication are written onto the relationship, `role` must be `service-provider` and `protocol` the profile's (both are in `consumerProviders` on `GET /admin-api/federation`), and the realm must have `federation.consumerProviders` on. |
| `role` | one of `service-provider`, `identity-provider` | yes | Which end THIS SERVICE is. `service-provider` means a foreign identity provider authenticates the person and this service consumes what it issues. |

**200**: The relationship as created, and what it still needs before it can be enabled usefully.

## POST /admin-api/federation/delete

`deleteFederationRelationship`

**Delete a relationship**

The entry goes and takes its recorded sign-ins with it. **The PEOPLE it authenticated keep their entries under `ou=users`** — nothing is ever deleted from there — and any session they hold is unaffected until it expires or is ended, which is what `POST /admin-api/logout` is for.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/federation` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | The relationship. |

**200**: Confirmation, and what was deliberately left behind.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `errors` | list |  |  |
| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `message` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean | yes |  |

**400**: The operation was refused; `errors` says why and nothing changed.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `errors` | list |  |  |
| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `message` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean | yes |  |

## POST /admin-api/federation/disable

`disableFederationRelationship`

**Turn a relationship off**

A response arriving for a disabled relationship is refused without being looked at, which is what disabling is for. Nothing else is lost: the configuration, the counters and the mappings all stay, and the people it authenticated keep their directory entries and their sessions.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/federation` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|

## POST /admin-api/federation/enable

`enableFederationRelationship`

**Turn a relationship on**

The second, deliberate act. **It is allowed on a relationship that is not fully configured**, and that is not a gap: a half-configured partner is a state somebody is passing through, and refusing to save it would mean configuring everything in one request with no way back. What happens in that state is that every endpoint for the relationship REFUSES and says which fields are missing — it never half-works — and the reply to this operation says so too.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/federation` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | The relationship. |

## POST /admin-api/federation/register-partner

`registerAtFederationPartner`

**Register this service at an OpenID Connect partner**

A relationship with `fedDiscovery` and `fedRegister` on (#930): reads the partner's discovery document and registers this relationship at its `registration_endpoint` (RFC 7591), writing the `client_id` and secret it answers to `fedClientId` and `fedClientSecret` (sealed) and the issuer to `fedRegisteredIssuer`. Registers again whatever client the relationship held.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/federation` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | The relationship. |

**200**: `clientId` and `issuer`.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clientId` | string |  |  |
| `errors` | list |  |  |
| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `issuer` | string |  |  |
| `message` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean | yes |  |

**400**: The operation was refused; `errors` says why and nothing changed.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clientId` | string |  |  |
| `errors` | list |  |  |
| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `issuer` | string |  |  |
| `message` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean | yes |  |

## POST /admin-api/federation/remove-value

`removeFederationValue`

Refused if that value is not there, rather than succeeding silently: a caller removing a mapping it thinks exists wants to hear that it does not.

## POST /admin-api/federation/rotate-key

`rotateFederationKey`

**Rotate a relationship's encryption key**

SAML 2.0, WS-Federation and OpenID Connect service-provider-side relationships only (#168). A new key of the relationship's `fedEncryptionKeyType` is issued under this realm's Intermediate and becomes CURRENT — what `/federation/metadata/{id}` and `/federation/jwks/{id}` publish. The key it replaces still DECRYPTS for `federation.encryptionKeyGraceS`, so a partner still holding the old certificate is not refused mid-change, and then decrypts nothing; the scheduler job `federation.encryption-key-retire` removes it. A second rotation inside that window drops the older key at once. Also the way to issue a key for a relationship that has none.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/federation` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | The relationship. |

**200**: The new key's kid, and the relationship as it now stands.

## POST /admin-api/federation/set

`setFederationField`

**Set one single-valued field on a relationship**

The field must be one of this relationship's — a field belonging to the other ROLE is refused by name rather than written and ignored, and so is one that records what HAPPENED (the counters, the last error).

`fedId`, `fedRole` and `fedProtocol` are refused too, and that is a third category rather than an oversight: they are the relationship's identity, and changing one would leave a SAML relationship carrying a token endpoint. Delete it and make another — there is no state to lose but the counters.

`GET /admin-api/federation?relationship=<id>` returns `editable`, which is exactly the list this operation accepts, so a caller need not guess.

The reply always carries `readiness`, so setting the last missing field tells you it was the last one.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/federation` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `field` | one of `fedName`, `fedPeer`, `fedLocalEntityId`, `fedEnabled`, `fedSsoUrl`, `fedTokenUrl`, `fedUserinfoUrl`, `fedJwksUri`, `fedEmailsUrl`, `fedJwks`, `fedTrustAnchor`, `fedSigningCertificate`, `fedClientId`, `fedClientSecret`, `fedResponseMode`, `fedTeamId`, `fedKeyId`, `fedClientSigningKey`, `fedTokenAuth`, `fedScope`, `fedResponseType`, `fedIdTokenSignedResponseAlg`, `fedUserinfoSignedResponseAlg`, `fedRefreshTokens`, `fedRefreshEverySeconds`, `fedRegister`, `fedRegisteredIssuer`, `fedRequestObject`, `fedRequestObjectSigningAlg`, `fedWebFinger`, `fedDiscovery`, `fedFapi`, `fedInitiateLogin`, `fedBinding`, `fedSignRequest`, `fedUsernameSource`, `fedSubjectClaim`, `fedAutocreateUsers`, `fedUpdateUserAttributes`, `fedProvisionGroups`, `fedProvisionCap`, `fedProvisionIdleMinutes`, `fedSubjectPolicy`, `fedSubjectPattern`, `fedMayAssertAdministrators`, `fedSignalEmailMatch`, `fedSignalsEnabled`, `fedSignalsIssuer`, `fedSignalsDelivery`, `fedSignalsTokenUrl`, `fedSignalsClientId`, `fedSignalsClientSecret`, `fedSignalsScope`, `fedSignalsBearer`, `fedSloUrl`, `fedSloBinding`, `fedEndSessionUrl`, `fedAcceptSignout`, `fedRequireSignedLogout`, `fedEncryptionKeyType`, `fedKeyManagementAlgorithm`, `fedContentEncryptionAlgorithm`, `fedAllowUnencrypted`, `fedAllowUnsolicited`, `fedApplication`, `fedAuthnMechanism`, `fedAuthnRelationship` | yes | The attribute name, e.g. `fedSsoUrl`, `fedSigningCertificate`, `fedClientId`. |
| `id` | string | yes | The relationship. |
| `value` | string | yes | The new value. An empty string clears it. `fedSigningCertificate` is normalised — PEM armour and whitespace are stripped, because what the schema holds is the base64 DER a ds:X509Certificate carries. |

## POST /admin-api/federation/signals-create-stream

`createFederationSignalsStream`

**Create this realm's stream at the partner**

SSF 1.0 section 8.1.1, discovering first where needed: a poll stream, or — `fedSignalsDelivery` push — a push stream to `/federation/signals/{id}` with an authorization header only this realm and the partner know. Asks for `fedSignalsEvents`. Audited.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/federation` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | The relationship. |

## POST /admin-api/federation/signals-discover

`discoverFederationSignals`

**Discover the partner's Shared Signals configuration**

Fetches `/.well-known/ssf-configuration` under the SSF issuer (`fedSignalsIssuer`, else `fedPeer`; SSF 1.0 section 7), which must name that issuer, a `jwks_uri` and a `configuration_endpoint`, and fetches the keys. Every address dialled afterwards is one that document named. Audited.

## POST /admin-api/federation/signals-poll-now

`pollFederationSignals`

**Poll the partner now**

RFC 8936, as the ssf.foreign-poll job does.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/federation` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

## POST /admin-api/federation/signals-read-status

`readFederationSignalsStatus`

**Read the stream's status from the partner**

SSF 1.0 section 8.1.2.1; the status is held and shown. Audited.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/federation` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | The relationship. |

## POST /admin-api/federation/signals-replace-stream

`replaceFederationSignalsStream`

**Replace the stream's configuration at the partner**

SSF 1.0 section 8.1.1.4: a PUT of the stream_id and every receiver-supplied property — the delivery the stream has, `fedSignalsEvents` as `events_requested`, the description. A push stream is given a new authorization header, held once the partner accepts it. Audited.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/federation` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | The relationship. |

## POST /admin-api/federation/signals-unblock

`unblockFederationSignals`

**Lift a partner's block on a person's sign-ins**

A verified `account-disabled` from a sign-in partner blocks its sign-ins of the person until its `account-enabled` (#373). This lifts the block by hand. Audited.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/federation` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | The relationship. |
| `user` | string | yes | The person. |

**200**: The relationship's Shared Signals as they stand.

## POST /admin-api/federation/signals-update-stream

`updateFederationSignalsStream`

**Send fedSignalsEvents to the stream**

A PATCH of `events_requested` to the relationship's `fedSignalsEvents`. Audited.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/federation` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | The relationship. |

## POST /admin-api/federation/signals-verify

`verifyFederationSignalsStream`

**Ask the partner for a verification event**

SSF 1.0 section 8.1.4.2: its state is checked when the event arrives.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/federation` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | The relationship. |
